an3.67:1.1: Also at [dn33:1.10.134](). A different ten at [an10.69](). | The phrase _kathāvatthu_ (“topics of discussion”) is best known from the eponymous book of the Abhidhamma, which details hundreds of points of doctrine that were contended among the early schools. | The purpose of debate is a major theme of the Aṭṭhakavagga ([snp4.3]() etc.).
an3.67:2.2: These are also at [an4.42](); see notes there.
an3.67:3.2: “What their position is and what it isn’t” (_ṭhānāṭhāne_): the commentary describes a debater who slips from one position to the next when challenged. | For consistency in “proposal” (_parikappa_) see [an10.177:10.1](). | For “procedure” (_paṭipadā_) the commentary gives the example of someone who asks questions at inappropriate times.
an3.67:6.3: These expressions probably refer to, respectively, the fourth, first, second, and third noble truths.
an3.67:12.4: The commentary connects _payuta_ with dropping hints and insinuations. However, its pre-Buddhist use shows that the root metaphor is “from (_pa-_) the yoke (_-yuta_)”: a cow wandering “astray” without cowherd (Rig Veda 10.27.8); fire “dispersed” in many fuels (3.55.4); a “scattered” mind (6.48.10, 7.100.2, 10.37.12); a “dismembered” enemy (5.32.2). Here it refers to speech that is “unhinged”, wandering without meaning.
